questions.stem: The 'Project Elephant', launched by the Government of India, was started in:
questions.explanation: Project Elephant was launched in February 1992 — nearly two decades after Project Tiger (1973). Goals: protect elephants, their habitats and corridors, address human-elephant conflict, restore migratory routes. India has about 33 notified Elephant Reserves and an estimated 27,000+ wild elephants (the largest population among Asian elephant countries). The Asian elephant (Elephas maximus) is the National Heritage Animal of India (declared 2010).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of India's three biodiversity 'hotspots' recognised internationally?
questions.explanation: Four of the world's 36 biodiversity hotspots extend into India — Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, and Sundaland (Nicobar Islands portion). The Thar desert is NOT a hotspot — hotspots require both high endemism (many unique species) AND severe habitat threat, which Thar's sparse biota does not meet. Hotspot criteria — 1,500+ endemic vascular plant species AND ≥ 70 % original habitat lost.

questions.stem: The 'Silent Valley National Park' is located in:
questions.explanation: Silent Valley is in Palakkad district, Kerala — a UNESCO tentative site within the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve. A proposed hydroelectric project here was scrapped after a major environmental movement in the late 1970s, partly due to threats to the lion-tailed macaque. Declared a National Park in 1984. Adjacent Mukurthi (TN) and Bandipur (Karnataka) are separately protected; Silent Valley sits in Kerala alone.

questions.stem: The difference between a National Park and a Wildlife Sanctuary in India is that:

options.option_text: A national park offers stricter protection — no human activity beyond research is allowed
Sanctuaries are always larger than national parks
Sanctuaries get central government funding; parks get state funding

questions.explanation: Under the Wildlife Protection Act 1972 — national parks (Section 35) have the strictest status: no grazing, no forest produce collection, no human habitation allowed (in principle). Sanctuaries (Section 18) allow some regulated human activities (controlled grazing, collection of forest produce in some cases) and still protect wildlife. Tiger reserves are a separate category — usually include both a core (park-level) area and a buffer (sanctuary-level).

questions.stem: The 'Great Indian Bustard', one of the most endangered birds in India, is the state bird of:
questions.explanation: The Great Indian Bustard (Ardeotis nigriceps) is the state bird of Rajasthan — locally 'Godawan'. IUCN-listed as Critically Endangered; estimated fewer than 150 birds remain in the wild. Major populations — Desert National Park (Rajasthan), pockets in Kachchh (Gujarat), Karera (MP). Big threat: collisions with high-voltage power lines in its flight corridors. Supreme Court in 2021 directed underground cabling in bustard habitats.

questions.stem: Which is India's first Marine National Park?

options.option_text: Gulf of Mannar Marine National Park
Gulf of Kachchh Marine National Park

questions.explanation: Gulf of Kachchh Marine National Park — Gujarat, established 1982 — was the first marine national park in India. Covers mangroves, coral reefs, mudflats and 42 islands. Gulf of Mannar (TN) was established as a biosphere reserve in 1989 (not originally a 'national park'). Mahatma Gandhi and Rani Jhansi marine parks are in the Andamans.

questions.stem: The term 'conservation reserve' in Indian wildlife law refers to:

options.option_text: A reserved forest managed only by the Forest Service
Buffer land adjoining a national park or sanctuary
An area where hunting is allowed under permit

questions.explanation: The Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2002 added two new categories: 'Conservation Reserve' (public-owned land adjoining existing parks / sanctuaries, serving as corridors or buffers) and 'Community Reserve' (private/community-owned land offered for conservation). These sit lower than parks / sanctuaries in restriction but give formal recognition. Example — Tiruppadaimarathur Conservation Reserve (Tamil Nadu), notified 2005, was India's first.
